result.summary: Вердикт FAIL, третий проход из трёх. Всё, что требовали прошлые проходы, теперь верно по моим собственным запускам: три канала отказа (событие, вопрос команды, строка ошибки) дают одну и ту же строку, мои 100 образцов «хранится» и 103 «отказ» сошлись с таблицей дизайна без единой ошибки, ровно 12 охранных тестов краснеют, все 42 мутанта дизайна убиты запланированными проверками, время линейное на 35 моих враждебных входах. Остался один блокирующий недочёт средней тяжести: правило «отбросить закрывающие скобки в конце значения» при естественной записи кода квадратично (4 МиБ знаков «)» после «token=» — 138 секунд при результате «секрета нет»), а ни одно из одиннадцати семейств прибора критерия 7 такого входа не содержит, поэтому тест этого не заметит. Починка маленькая и местная (одно предложение в правиле, одно семейство, один мутант), но по условию третий FAIL останавливает требование: что делать дальше, решает ORCH и владелец.

findings.pass_item: pass A item 3 (mutants of the design, hostile input), pass D item 9 (Q10), criterion 7; quality-bar section 6 item 1 (a green run where the property cannot break proves nothing)
findings.place: design section 2.2 item 3 (the sentence on trailing `)`, `]`, `}`), item 5 and its cost paragraph (only groups are argued), item 6 (the list of one-pass helpers does not name this step), section 10 (families 1-11), section 9 row Q10 ('hostile input is linear (families 1-11...)'), section 11 (no mutant), section 12 G-1, G-2, G-7, G-8
findings.what: The written rule 'trailing `)`, `]`, `}` that have no opener of their own kind inside the value are dropped' is linear only if the presence of each opener kind is looked up once. A natural reading of the text (drop one closer, look for its opener in the rest of the value, repeat) re-scans the value for every dropped closer. I wrote my re-implementation from the design text and the requirement block this way, without noticing the trap: it returns exactly the oracle (100 kept, 103 refused, no wrong form), passes all eleven families of my copy of the instrument of section 10 (worst ratio 4.10, no false failure, total 71.5 s), and is quadratic on a value that is a long run of one closer: `token=` followed by `)` x N returns 'no secret' after 0.54 s at 256 KiB, 2.1 s at 512 KiB, 8.6 s at 1 MiB and 137.9 s at 4 MiB (x4 per doubling; `}` and `]` the same). The designer's own sketch is linear on the same input (88 ms and 170 ms at 4 MiB for `)` and `}`), so the rule is not wrong: the design neither says that this step must be single-pass nor has any family or mutant that would show a re-scan. An implementation that re-scans passes every planned test, and the core would stall for minutes in the synchronous `#publish` on a 5 MiB file of closers (Q10, criterion 7 'linear time'). This is the same class as F11, F12 and G1 of the earlier passes (a hostile shape found one at a time); the family list is the only guard.
findings.needed: Say in section 2.2 that dropping trailing closers is one pass in which each opener kind is looked up once (no re-scan per dropped closer) and add the step to the helpers named in item 6; add a family of the instrument for a value that is `token=` plus a long run of a closer (with the two outcomes per size: no secret, bait at the end found; the three sizes; the ratio below 8) and one mutant 'the value is re-scanned for every dropped closer' that this family kills; carry the new family count, the mutant and the new budget into section 10, section 11 and the micro-amendment G (G-1, G-2, G-7, G-8) and into section 9 row Q10. The budget has room: eleven families and the control cost 71.5 s of 120 s on my run, one more family is about 5 s. No ready text is given here.
